record.original_question: Within anisotropic function spaces adapted to hydrodynamics, what is the true regularity of generalized minimal flows?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a two-dimensional ideal incompressible fluid governed by the Euler equations, and let a generalized minimal flow (GM-flow) denote a stationary solution whose stream function is a minimizer of the Dirichlet energy under prescribed area-preserving rearrangement constraints on the vorticity. Such flows are known to possess analytic level lines of vorticity along the direction of streamlines, while exhibiting only finite (transversal) regularity across streamlines. Introduce anisotropic function spaces adapted to hydrodynamics, namely spaces in which the regularity index along the flow direction is allowed to be larger than the regularity index in the transversal direction (for example, anisotropic Hölder, Sobolev, or Besov spaces with two distinct smoothness exponents tied to the local frame of streamlines).

Problem. Determine the true (sharp) regularity of generalized minimal flows in such anisotropic function spaces. That is, identify the optimal pair of smoothness exponents (longitudinal regularity along streamlines, transversal regularity across streamlines) such that every GM-flow belongs to the corresponding anisotropic space, and construct examples showing the exponents cannot be improved.
artifact.category_tag: Regularity of stationary Euler flows in anisotropic spaces
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of determining the sharp regularity of generalized minimal flows in anisotropic function spaces adapted to hydrodynamics is posed as an open problem in the geometric hydrodynamics open-problems collection. No subsequent solution or sharp regularity result for GM-flows in such anisotropic spaces appears in the available literature.

status_evidence.title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: GM-flows have natural, intrinsic structure with analytic level lines of vorticity and finite regularity in the transversal direction; the suitable functional classes are an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The regularity of GM-flows in anisotropic function spaces is listed as an open problem.
